title: Coherence of normalized shifted Tate-unit comparisons
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $S$, finite coefficient extensions $\mathbf Q_\ell=E_0\subset E\subset F$ with their valuation rings [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and an integer $d\ge0$. Work on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $R_L=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,S}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], $U_L=R_L[0]$, and $T_L=U_L(d)[2d]$, using [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let $A=C_{E/E_0,S}$, $B=C_{F/E,S}$ and $D=C_{F/E_0,S}$ be ordinary derived coefficient extensions $C_{H/L,S}(K)=K\otimes^L_{R_L}R_H$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], identified on derived-complete objects with the strict-tower extensions of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] by the specified natural comparison $\chi$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Let $\alpha:BA\xrightarrow{\sim}D$ be the natural ordinary tensor associator, with this normalization under $\chi$.
For $L\subset H$ among the three fields let $u_{H/L}:C_{H/L,S}U_L\xrightarrow{\sim}U_H$ be the derived coefficient-unit multiplication: it is induced by the degree-zero module-sheaf map $x\otimes b\mapsto\iota_{H/L}(x)b$ and the canonical K-flat resolving comparison, where $\iota_{H/L}:R_L\to R_H$ is the coefficient inclusion. Let $s_{H/L,K,n}:C_{H/L,S}(K[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(C_{H/L,S}K)[n]$ be the canonical shift comparison induced by termwise change of rings. Let $\beta_{H/L,K}:C_{H/L,S}(K(d))\xrightarrow{\sim}(C_{H/L,S}K)(d)$ be the specified natural twist comparison of [lem-weil-integral-twist-derived-scalar]. Define
$$q_{H/L}=(u_{H/L}(d)\circ\beta_{H/L,U_L})[2d]\circ s_{H/L,U_L(d),2d}:C_{H/L,S}T_L\xrightarrow{\sim}T_H.$$
The objects $U_L,T_L$ belong to the derived-complete integral constructible finite-Tor categories [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The uniform Tor intervals of $U_L,T_L$ are respectively $[0,0]$ and $[-2d,-2d]$. Also $AT_0$ belongs to the same category at $E$. With $u_E=u_{E/E_0}$, $u_F=u_{F/E_0}$, $v=u_{F/E}$, $\theta_E=q_{E/E_0}$, $\theta_F=q_{F/E_0}$ and $a=q_{F/E}$, the specified maps satisfy
$$u_F\circ\alpha_{U_0}=v\circ B(u_E),\qquad \theta_F\circ\alpha_{T_0}=a\circ B(\theta_E).$$
These equalities use the canonical shift comparisons displayed above, and hold also for identity coefficient extensions.

proof.text: Write $J_L=\mathcal O_L(d)$ for the unshifted Tate line. By prop-weil-twist-preserves, $J_L$ is locally free of rank one over $R_L$. Tensoring a complex with $R_L[0]$ is the identity, and tensoring with $J_L[0]$ is locally the identity; both therefore take acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes. By the definition of K-flatness, these degree-zero complexes, and their shifts, are K-flat with flat terms. The derived-change-of-rings computation thus uses these very complexes as their own resolutions. In particular all ordinary scalar comparisons below are represented by the displayed module maps, with no auxiliary choices. The specified natural comparison $\chi$ identifies this computation with the strict-tower functors on complete inputs; its finite-freeness assertion applies to every coefficient inclusion, including repeated fields.

source.place: Agent calculation implementing coefficient transport, Step 3 of sk-thm-purity-transport

proof.text: For each $L$, clause 2 of lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible gives derived completeness and bounded constructibility of $U_L$, with its actual derived reductions $(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^j)_S[0]$ for every $j\geq1$. Tensoring such a reduction with any module sheaf $M[0]$ is $M[0]$ by coefficient multiplication. Thus its Tor interval is $[0,0]$, independent of $j$, which is precisely the integral finite-Tor condition in def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude. No equality of cohomological support with $\{0\}$ is needed.

source.place: Agent calculation implementing coefficient transport, Step 3 of sk-thm-purity-transport

proof.text: Apply prop-weil-twist-preserves to $U_L$ with twist $d$: $U_L(d)$ is derived complete and constructible, and its reductions retain Tor interval $[0,0]$. Closure under shifts in lem-weil-integral-ctf-triangulated gives $T_L=U_L(d)[2d]$ in the integral constructible finite-Tor category. More explicitly, reduction commutes with this canonical shift, and for each finite coefficient module $M$, the tensor of the reduced $T_L$ with $M[0]$ is the corresponding line-tensor module placed in degree $-2d$. The uniform interval is therefore $[-2d,-2d]$. This is a containing Tor interval also when $S$ is empty.

source.place: Agent calculation implementing coefficient transport, Step 3 of sk-thm-purity-transport

proof.text: On the degree-zero models of step 1, $u_{H/L}$ is multiplication $x\otimes b\mapsto\iota_{H/L}(x)b$, with inverse $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. The ordinary associator sends $(x\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $x\otimes\iota_{F/E}(b)c$. Consequently $u_F\alpha_{U_0}$ sends this tensor to $\iota_{F/E_0}(x)\iota_{F/E}(b)c$, and $vB(u_E)$ sends it to $\iota_{F/E}(\iota_{E/E_0}(x)b)c$, the same section since coefficient inclusions compose. Equality on pure tensors gives equality on tensor presheaves and hence their sheafifications and derived images. The resolving comparison is the canonical one from step 1, so this proves the equation for the specified $u$ maps.

source.place: Agent calculation implementing coefficient transport, Step 3 of sk-thm-purity-transport

proof.text: Let $b_{H/L}:J_L\otimes_{R_L}R_H\to J_H$ be the canonical twist-line base change of lem-weil-integral-twist-base-change. Put $w_{H/L}=u_{H/L}(d)\beta_{H/L,U_L}$ before shifting. The termwise formula in lem-weil-integral-twist-derived-scalar identifies this composite with $(x\otimes l)\otimes b\mapsto\iota_{H/L}(x)b\,b_{H/L}(l\otimes1)$, using the coefficient action $R_H\otimes J_H\cong J_H$. In the tower, $w_{F/E_0}\alpha_{U_0(d)}$ on $((x\otimes l)\otimes b)\otimes c$ has value $\iota_{F/E_0}(x)\iota_{F/E}(b)c\,b_{F/E_0}(l\otimes1)$. The successive path $w_{F/E}B(w_{E/E_0})$ has value $\iota_{F/E_0}(x)\iota_{F/E}(b)c\,b_{F/E}(b_{E/E_0}(l\otimes1)\otimes1)$. These are equal by the tower compatibility explicitly asserted for $b$. The same pure-tensor/sheafification argument proves equality of these unshifted maps. Each $w$ is an isomorphism since both its factors are.

source.place: Agent calculation implementing coefficient transport, Step 3 of sk-thm-purity-transport

proof.text: Take $n=2d$. On a complex $P$, termwise coefficient extension identifies $(P[n])^r\otimes R_H=P^{r+n}\otimes R_H=(P\otimes R_H)[n]^r$ by the identity on tensors, which also respects the differential $(-1)^n d_P\otimes1$. Thus the specified $s$ is exactly this comparison. For two extensions, applying these identity component maps twice and then $\alpha_P[n]$ gives $\alpha_{P[n]}$ followed by the direct shift comparison: both send $(z\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $z\otimes\iota_{F/E}(b)c$. The same component calculation commutes with each $w$. Shift the equality of step 5 using these identities. Its direct composite is $q_{F/E_0}\alpha_{T_0}$, and its successive composite is $q_{F/E}B(q_{E/E_0})$, by the defining formula for $q$. The equality is for the specified completed normalization as well: the chain-shift compatibility of the actual quotient-map comparison $\chi$ is precisely lem-weil-completed-scalar-chain-shift. No inverse to $\chi$ at chain level is used.

source.place: Agent calculation implementing coefficient transport, Step 3 of sk-thm-purity-transport

proof.text: The composite defining $q_{H/L}$ is an isomorphism, so $AT_0\cong T_E$ by $q_{E/E_0}$. The isomorphism-closure in lem-weil-integral-ctf-triangulated and step 3 put $AT_0$ in the required category. For an identity coefficient extension, multiplication $x\otimes b\mapsto xb$ is the canonical coefficient unitor, $b_{L/L}$ is the tensor-power unitor (the zero twist is coefficient multiplication), and $s$ is the componentwise comparison of step 6. In the formulas of steps 4 and 5 replace the relevant inclusion by the identity; the same products and the same tensor-power maps result on both paths. Hence both equations include repeated fields. Under $\chi$ the identity functor is identified by the natural completeness map, as specified by lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison, rather than assumed strictly equal to its completion.
